analysis.evidence: The subject is גְּבוּל הַכְּנַעֲנִי, “the boundary of the Canaanites.” The phrases beginning with מִצִּידֹן, “from Sidon,” trace its course. In context, “the boundary ran from Sidon” expresses this spatial use of “was.”
analysis.morphology: The prefixed conjunction וַ precedes יְהִי, the shortened Qal wayyiqtol form, third masculine singular. The verb agrees with גְּבוּל, “boundary.”
analysis.sense: to be in a state or condition

analysis.evidence: גְּבוּל הַכְּנַעֲנִי means “the boundary of the Canaanites.” The verse traces its course from Sidon (מִצִּידֹן), using עַד to mark how far it extends.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular common noun in the construct state, with הַכְּנַעֲנִי as its complement.

analysis.evidence: גְּבוּל הַכְּנַעֲנִי means “the boundary of the Canaanites.” The description traces that boundary from Sidon, identifying the people whose territory it encloses.
analysis.morphology: The definite article הַ precedes a masculine singular absolute gentilic used collectively.

draft.change: Add a geographical sense for צִידוֹן and correct the occurrence gloss from “Zebulun” to “from Sidon.”
draft.definition: Sidon is the city from which the description of the Canaanite boundary begins.
draft.evidence: Genesis 10:19 places Sidon at the starting point of the boundary by prefixing מִן to the name.

analysis.evidence: גְּבוּל הַכְּנַעֲנִי identifies the subject as the Canaanite boundary. מִצִּידֹן gives its starting point, and the following phrases trace its course toward Gerar and as far as Gaza.
analysis.morphology: The preposition מִן means “from.” Its nun assimilates to the initial צ of the proper name, producing the dagesh in צּ. The name is written here with ḥolam on ד.

analysis.evidence: The boundary starts at Sidon. The directional ending on גְרָרָה gives the heading ‘toward Gerar’, and עַד עַזָּה gives the limit ‘as far as Gaza’. The verse repeats בֹּאֲכָה with סְדֹמָה to describe the direction toward Sodom.
analysis.morphology: Qal infinitive construct with a second-person masculine singular suffix. The suffix supplies the subject of the motion, a generic ‘you’ following the route.

analysis.evidence: The verse traces the Canaanite boundary from Sidon toward Gerar. עַד עַזָּה marks Gaza as the endpoint of this stretch.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew preposition without a prefix or suffix. Its complement is the place name עַזָּה.
analysis.sense: as far as, up to, to (a place or person)

draft.change: Add a place-name entry for עַזָּה under nouns/, using the name’s consonants עזה as its filing root. Replace the source gloss “hiss” with “Gaza.”
draft.definition: Gaza, a city marking a limit of Canaanite territory.
draft.evidence: Genesis 10:19 names Gaza as the point the boundary reaches on the way toward Gerar.

analysis.evidence: In the description of Canaanite territory, עַד עַזָּה means “as far as Gaza.” The parallel עַד לָשַׁע, “as far as Lasha,” identifies another boundary point.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew proper noun. The final ה belongs to the place name. The preceding עַד is a separate preposition.

analysis.evidence: In בֹּאֲכָה סְדֹמָה, the directional ending on סְדֹמָה gives the sense “toward Sodom.” The phrase parallels the earlier בֹּאֲכָה גְרָרָה, “as you come toward Gerar,” in tracing the Canaanite boundary.
analysis.morphology: Qal infinitive construct with a second-person masculine singular suffix. The suffix supplies the subject, a generic “you.”

draft.change: Add a standalone place-name article for סְדֹם, keyed by its own consonants סדמ. The supplied root סגר does not account for this form.
draft.definition: סְדֹם is the Hebrew name of the city of Sodom.
draft.evidence: Genesis 10:19 names Sodom alongside Gomorrah, Admah, and Zeboiim in its description of Canaanite territory.

analysis.evidence: The boundary description repeats בֹּאֲכָה, “as you go.” The first occurrence introduces the direction toward Gerar, גְרָרָה, and the second introduces the direction toward Sodom, סְדֹמָה. Both place names carry directional ־ָה.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew proper noun with the directional suffix ־ָה, marking Sodom as a destination.
